subject: Regional continuity carve-in request: active-active switchover commitments
messages:
From: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@latticebank.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: LatticeBank Ops <ops@latticebank.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: guaranteed switchover times for multi-region continuity

Hi Priyom,

Following up from our SRE sync — LatticeBank is updating its customer-facing uptime commitments and we need firm guarantees for active-region failover. Specifically:
- Objective: end-to-end switchover for API traffic between us-east and us-west within an RTO of 2 minutes and RPO of <=30s for user-facing endpoints.
- Scope: production traffic for our payment-validation route (~10k qps peak), active-active with automated health-based routing.

We understand this is outside your standard SLA. Can Redwood provide an exception (carve-in) to guarantee those commitments, or propose an alternative with clear trade-offs? We also need a draft runbook and a list of required operational changes on our side.

Attaching a short request summary. Let me know if we should route this to an account exec or SRE directly.

Thanks,
Samantha Reed
Director, Platform Operations
LatticeBank

Attachments: lattice-request-summary.pdf

Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: guaranteed switchover times for multi-region continuity

Team — forwarding LatticeBank's ask. TL;DR: RTO 2m / RPO 30s for a high-throughput payments route. This is well beyond our standard failover commitment. Need a quick read on feasibility, estimated infra changes, and an outline of commercial terms we can offer (penalty, limited window, or reduced throughput clause).

Specific asks:
- Marissa: feasibility + runbook gaps and whether active-active health-based routing can meet 2m at 10k qps (assuming KV cache priming).
- Aditya: cost estimate for reserved warm capacity (east+west) and whether we need dedicated reserved nodes vs burst pools.
- Markus: legal input on how to structure a timeboxed SLA exception and proposed liability cap.

Goal: quick internal alignment, then propose a scoped offer to Lattice by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Priyom
Head of Sales (Enterprise)
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: guaranteed switchover times for multi-region continuity

On Sat, Aug 22, 2026 at 10:02 AM priyom.das@redwood.com wrote:
> Team — forwarding LatticeBank's ask.

I ran an initial ops assessment. Short answer: 2m RTO @10k qps is achievable only with the following constraints and investments:

- Active-active pre-warmed state: we must keep KV caches primed in both regions and ensure consistent prefix caching. That requires persistent warm workers per shard (not just burst).
- Network-level routing: health-based DNS failover won't meet 2m on its own unless we use edge-level anycast + immediate route announcements and a pre-propagated fallback routing policy.
- Sequencing and consistency: for payments, we need to guarantee leaderless idempotency and accept eventual leader reconcile for a short window — implies application changes on Lattice (idempotency keys + duplicate-detection window).

Estimated deliverables and lead times:
- Runbook draft (attached) — outlines steps for automated switchover, manual rollback, postmortem exercises. (see proposed-runbook.pdf)
- Infra changes: dedicated warm pool (east+west) per shard and prioritized preemption policy — 3–4 weeks to provision and test end-to-end; 2 weeks if customer accepts limited throughput (throttle to 6k qps) during initial rollout.
- SLO construct: we can offer an SLA exception for an RTO of 10 minutes with RPO 60s on our standard terms. To get to 2m/30s we'd need a bespoke engineering program and commercial commitments (revenue tier + reserved capacity).

I'll attach a runbook draft and a checklist for customer-side changes. Happy to join a joint ops call with Lattice next week.

-Marissa
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-runbook.pdf
From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@latticebank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: guaranteed switchover times for multi-region continuity

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear ask and patience while we assessed. Quick summary of our internal position and a proposal for moving forward:

1) Off-the-shelf: Redwood can commit to a scoped exception with RTO 10 minutes / RPO 60s for the payments route under our standard commercial terms plus a one-time mitigation fee. This requires Lattice to adopt the idempotency and traffic-pattern controls in the attached checklist.

2) Bespoke fast-failover program: If Lattice requires the 2m/30s guarantees, we propose a short program: 6-week engineering engagement + reserved east+west warm capacity + joint SRE runbooks. Commercials: reserved capacity commitment (12 months) + higher SLA premium. We can produce a term-sheet if you want to pursue.

3) Risk & liability: Markus, can you prepare a limited-term SLA exception term-sheet that includes a revenue-based liability cap and an operational carve-in window (business hours only for the first 90 days)?

Next steps:
- Samantha, confirm whether Lattice prefers the scoped exception (10m/60s) to get baseline coverage quickly, or to kick off the fast-failover program.
- Marissa to schedule a joint ops workshop to align runbook and customer app changes.

I will follow up with a draft term-sheet once Markus provides legal language.

Best,
Priyom
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@latticebank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: guaranteed switchover times for multi-region continuity

Samantha / Priyom — attaching a short term-sheet (sla-exception-term-sheet.docx) that codifies the scoped exception offer: RTO 10 minutes / RPO 60s, 90-day probation window, business-hours carve-in for initial 30 days, liability cap equal to 6 months of committed fees, and an obligation to complete the joint ops runbook and an initial chaos test within 45 days.

If Lattice signs the term-sheet we will open an SRE ticket and schedule a canary run with staged throttles. We recommend a pilot on non-critical traffic for 2 weeks before full production switchover.

Samantha — please review and let us know if legal needs any additional clarifications. Happy to hop on a call to walk through the clauses.

-Markus
VP Legal, Redwood Inference

Attachments: sla-exception-term-sheet.docx
